The Wolves now have $124 million committed to the 26-year-old over the next four years. McDaniels averaged a career-high 14.8 points last season and is the team's top perimeter defender.
items.impact: No direct effect on Chad's teams; it is a league-wide signing ahead of opening night.

items.headline: World Series set: Rays vs. Brewers, Game 1 Friday at 7 PM CT on FOX
items.summary_html: The World Series starts tied 0-0 with Tampa Bay at Milwaukee on Friday, October 23, at 7 PM CT on FOX, and Game 2 is Saturday at the same time. Milwaukee (103-59) has home-field advantage over Tampa Bay (98-64). Games 3 through 5 are in Tampa Bay from October 26 to 28, and a Game 7, if needed, would be Saturday, October 31, in Milwaukee.
items.connections: The Brewers swept the Dodgers in the NLCS and the Rays beat the Guardians 4-2 in the ALCS. Both franchises are among five that have never won a World Series.
items.impact: Every game starts at 7 PM CT on FOX, so it fits after work and church evenings for Chad.

items.headline: Families say upkeep has slipped at Crestview Cemetery in Gallatin
items.summary_html: People with loved ones buried at Crestview Cemetery in Gallatin told WSMV they've been cleaning gravesites themselves, pointing to weeds on headstones, downed limbs on graves, and a cross that needs paint. They said upkeep declined after management changed a few years ago and their complaints haven't brought fixes. WSMV sent Crestview questions and had no response.
items.impact: This is a Sumner County community story and doesn't directly affect Chad unless his family has someone buried at Crestview.

items.headline: Family of DoorDash driver killed on North Dupont Avenue asks for justice as three gunmen remain unidentified
items.summary_html: Police say 22-year-old John and his 14-year-old brother Alan were sitting in a car at Birchstone Village Apartments on North Dupont Avenue around 7:45 PM last Thursday when three men approached and opened fire. John died at Skyline Medical Center, and Alan, who was shot in the head, is awake and recovering at Vanderbilt, according to their mother. Homicide detectives say they are pursuing strong leads to identify the three suspects, and Crime Stoppers is at 615-742-7463.
items.connections: This is the same North Dupont Avenue shooting covered in last week's local sections, and the three suspects are still at large.
items.impact: North Dupont Avenue is in Madison, along the Nashville side of Chad's route between Hendersonville and the city. It doesn't change his plans, but the suspects haven't been caught.

items.headline: Trump announces $8 billion diesel relief program for farmers at Kansas rally
items.summary_html: At a Monday night rally for Sen. Roger Marshall in Kansas, Trump announced a USDA Harvest Fuel Relief Program offering $8 billion in one-time payments to help farmers offset diesel costs this harvest. USDA said payments will use a uniform formula based on modeled 2026 crop-year losses, run through the Farm Service Agency, with Title I payment rates due in November and no application dates set yet.
items.connections: The Hill reports diesel averages about $6.32 a gallon per AAA, up from $3.63 a year ago, amid the Iran war, and farm-state Republicans had pressed for relief. Marshall faces Democrat Adam Hamilton, a Methodist pastor who has proposed suspending federal fuel taxes until the Iran conflict ends.
items.impact: Chad isn't a farmer, so he wouldn't get these payments. The high fuel prices behind the program are the same ones he pays driving to church.

items.headline: Aaron Boone will return as Yankees manager in 2027
items.summary_html: Aaron Boone will be back for his 10th season managing the Yankees in 2027, a source confirmed to ESPN on Monday, the final year of his current contract. New York was swept by Tampa Bay in the ALDS, its second straight Division Series exit, and hasn't won a World Series since 2009.
items.connections: The Rays team that swept the Yankees led Cleveland 3-2 in the ALCS going into Monday night's Game 6.
items.impact: League-wide MLB news; no effect on Chad's daily life.

items.headline: Rams' Davante Adams out 6-10 weeks with ruptured hamstring
items.summary_html: Rams receiver Davante Adams will miss six to 10 weeks after rupturing a hamstring late in Sunday's 18-16 loss to Arizona and will have surgery, coach Sean McVay said Monday. McVay also said nose tackle Poona Ford is out for the season with a ruptured triceps, Kobie Turner will miss a handful of weeks with a groin injury, and kicker Blake Grupe tore an ACL and went on injured reserve.
items.impact: League-wide NFL injury news; no direct effect on the Titans or Chad.

items.headline: Bucks waive Kevin Porter Jr. ahead of opener
items.summary_html: Milwaukee waived guard Kevin Porter Jr. on Monday ahead of the NBA roster deadline. Porter led the Bucks in assists last season, averaging 17.4 points and 7.4 assists in 38 games. Milwaukee, in its first season since trading Giannis Antetokounmpo to Miami, opens Wednesday at Washington.
items.connections: It was one of several cuts on deadline day, including Dallas waiving Dwight Powell after 12 seasons and the Lakers waiving Dalton Knecht.
items.impact: League-wide NBA news; no effect on the Mavericks or Chad.

items.headline: UK regulator proposes forcing Apple to open iPhone contactless tech to rival wallets
items.summary_html: The UK Competition and Markets Authority opened a consultation on Oct 20 proposing that Apple give businesses access to the iPhone's NFC contactless chip through both main international standards, secure element and host card emulation, instead of only secure element as today. The CMA expects access fees to be substantially lower than Apple's current charges, though it is not setting prices itself. The consultation closes Nov 17, 2026.
items.connections: The CMA notes that in the EU, where Apple agreed to provide NFC payment access, Vipps, PayPal, Klarna, Curve and BBVA launched alternative wallet apps, while no rival wallet has launched in the UK. The proposal is a conduct requirement under the UK's digital markets law, following Apple's Strategic Market Status designation.
items.impact: This applies to the UK only, so it doesn't change how Apple Pay or the Wallet app work on Chad's iPhone in Tennessee.

items.headline: Nashville police search for man accused of attacking ex-girlfriend with hammer
items.summary_html: Metro police are searching for 38-year-old Ross Peterson, who faces warrants for aggravated assault, harassment and theft after a woman he had previously dated was found with severe head and face injuries in her backyard around 7:15 AM Saturday. Officers had helped her get an order of protection and a harassment warrant hours earlier, and police say Peterson came back to the home and attacked her after she confronted him. Anyone who sees him is asked to call Crime Stoppers at 615-742-7463.
items.impact: The suspect is still at large in Davidson County, but the article gives no neighborhood, and nothing ties it to Hendersonville, Chad's schools, or his church route.

items.headline: OpenAI says its newest models can now build and migrate COBOL, Fortran and Visual Basic code
items.summary_html: OpenAI said on Oct 19 that its latest models are much better at older, low-resource programming languages that banks and governments still rely on. On its new MultiLangBench test, GPT-6 Astra passed 87.4% across 20 languages versus 26.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol, and GPT-6.1 Sol reached 97.9% accuracy on COBOL-to-modern-language migration at high reasoning effort. OpenAI notes production migrations still need expert review and full testing.
items.impact: This doesn't touch Chad's daily life; it mainly matters to banks and agencies modernizing old systems.

items.headline: Seven 2023 draftees sign rookie extensions; Brandon Miller gets $209M
items.summary_html: Seven 2023 first-round picks signed rookie-scale extensions before Monday's deadline, led by Victor Wembanyama (5 years, $252M), Brandon Miller (5 years, $209M, agreed Monday with Charlotte) and Amen Thompson (5 years, $208M). Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George, Cason Wallace and Brandin Podziemski also signed. Players who didn't sign become restricted free agents in 2027.
items.connections: Dallas' Dereck Lively II, also from the 2023 class, was not extended. The regular season opens Tuesday, Oct. 20.
items.impact: League-wide NBA news; no direct effect on Chad.

items.headline: General Jackson Showboat to retire after 41 years on the Cumberland
items.summary_html: Opry Entertainment Group says it will retire the General Jackson Showboat because ongoing maintenance problems have disrupted its operating schedule. The four-deck paddle-wheel boat has sailed the Cumberland River near Opryland since 1985. The company says all dates currently on its public cruise calendar are still expected to sail.
items.impact: No effect on Chad's drive or schools, but anyone wanting a last cruise should book from the dates still on the calendar.

items.headline: Mavericks pass on Dereck Lively II extension at deadline
items.summary_html: Dallas did not sign Dereck Lively II to a rookie-scale extension before Monday's 5 p.m. CT deadline, so he plays 2026-27 on the final year of his rookie deal ($7,239,131). The Mavs can make him a restricted free agent next summer and match any offer. Lively, who had right foot surgery in December, still isn't medically cleared and will miss Wednesday's opener at Houston.
items.connections: It came the same day Dallas waived Dwight Powell after 12 seasons, leaving Daniel Gafford as the only center healthy throughout camp. Santi Aldama is also uncertain for the opener.
items.impact: Mavs news for Chad as a fan; it doesn't touch his budget or daily life.

items.headline: At least three teams in the mix for suspended Jets goalie Connor Hellebuyck
items.summary_html: At least three teams remain in talks to trade for Winnipeg goalie Connor Hellebuyck, ESPN reported Monday, though a deal isn't guaranteed before his team-issued suspension ends Friday, Oct. 23. Hellebuyck, the 2025 Hart Trophy winner, requested a trade this summer and was suspended for not reporting to camp; he has forfeited nearly $800,000 so far and holds a full no-movement clause.
items.impact: League-wide NHL news; no report ties the Predators to a trade.

items.headline: Senate Democrats demand answers from SpaceX on Ukraine's Starlink and Starshield restrictions
items.summary_html: Senators Jeanne Shaheen, Richard Blumenthal, Sheldon Whitehouse and Chris Coons sent a letter to SpaceX legal VP Christopher Cardaci asking who decided to restrict Ukraine's Starshield access for devices moving faster than 100 mph starting October 14, and what role SpaceX plays. They asked for answers, records and Starshield contracts by November 2. The same day, Zelensky told a bipartisan group of lawmakers that Starlink and Starshield services were still speed-restricted in parts of the front.
items.connections: This follows last week's Reuters and CNBC reports that the White House ordered Starshield speed limits on Ukraine military terminals, which Musk said the US military and the president control. It lands one day before SpaceX reports its third-quarter results on October 20.
items.impact: It doesn't touch Chad's daily life directly, but it raises political pressure on SpaceX right before its earnings call, which matters if he follows the stock or Starlink's government business.

items.headline: Predators 3-2-3 after eight games, head to Boston and Pittsburgh this week
items.summary_html: Nashville is 3-2-3 with nine points through eight games, tied for fifth in the Central Division. The Predators rank fourth in the NHL on the power play at 29.6 percent and seventh on the penalty kill at 85.2 percent, and Juuse Saros has started seven of the eight games. They play at Boston on Thursday and at Pittsburgh on Saturday.
items.connections: The road trip follows Saturday's 5-2 home win over St. Louis, which closed a three-game homestand.
items.impact: Both road games start at 6 PM CT, Thursday October 22 at Boston and Saturday October 24 at Pittsburgh, and the Preds return home Sunday October 25 against Colorado.

items.headline: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts expected to miss rest of season with blood clots in lungs
items.summary_html: Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season after doctors found deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in both lungs, according to a statement from the Eagles and his agent, Nicole Lynn. Sources told ESPN and NFL Network he'll be on blood thinners for at least three months. A clot first found before the Eagles' Week 5 game in London later moved, and he's now on injured reserve.
items.connections: Hurts sat out Sunday's Week 6 game against Carolina after a follow-up ultrasound showed the clot had moved.
items.impact: League-wide NFL news; it doesn't affect the Titans' schedule or Chad's daily life.

items.headline: Anthropic in talks for a second $45B compute deal with Nscale
items.summary_html: Bloomberg News reported on Oct 19, per Reuters, that Nscale is negotiating to sell Anthropic computing power from a second building at its Monarch data center campus in West Virginia, in a deal that could be worth about $45 billion. The building would deliver 460 megawatts using Nvidia Vera Rubin chips, on top of the $45 billion deal Anthropic signed in August for the first building. Neither company commented, Reuters could not verify the report, and details could still change.
items.connections: The talks come right after Microsoft pulled out of anchoring Nscale's Essex, UK data center over grid delays, and days after Anthropic announced its Public Benefit Fund.
items.impact: Nothing changes for Chad directly. It signals Anthropic is still buying large amounts of compute, which supports Claude capacity over time.

items.headline: Justice Department charges 28 California green card holders with voter fraud
items.summary_html: The Justice Department charged 28 lawful permanent residents in California, accusing them of falsely claiming U.S. citizenship to register to vote, with many allegedly casting ballots, and of lying about it later on naturalization applications. Eleven were arrested Monday. The charges, false statements in a naturalization application and in some cases fraudulent voter registration, carry up to five years in federal prison each.
items.connections: The charges follow the administration's lawsuit against California seeking to set aside mail ballots from people it identified as likely noncitizens. Democrats and voting rights groups call the push an effort to sow doubt in the Nov. 3 midterms, while Stephen Miller says courts have blocked federal efforts to check voter rolls against federal databases.
items.impact: No direct effect on Chad, since the charges are in California; it's part of the national fight over voter eligibility rules ahead of the Nov. 3 election he'll vote in.

items.headline: 18-year-old jailed after 100 mph chase ends in crash at Nolensville Pike and Edmondson Pike
items.summary_html: Metro police say 18-year-old Eric Escalante drove more than 100 mph through the Nolensville Pike area Saturday night, running red lights and crossing into oncoming lanes, before hitting a Toyota sedan at Nolensville Pike and Edmondson Pike and injuring four people. Police say he then grabbed a rifle and ran into the woods before surrendering. He is jailed on a $126,000 bond on charges including four counts of aggravated assault, drag racing and evading arrest.
items.impact: This happened in south Nashville, well off Chad's Hendersonville routes and his drive to Priest Lake, so it doesn't directly affect him.

items.headline: Grok Bot now works with the iPhone Action Button
items.summary_html: Grok Bot's official X account said on Oct 19 that iPhone users can set Grok Bot as the Action Button, so one press starts a live voice chat with their Bot without opening the app. It needs the Grok Bot iOS app version 1.16 on an iPhone 15 Pro or later; in Settings, Action Button, users swipe to Shortcut and choose Grok Bot, Start Voice Chat. The feature comes three days after Friday's Grok Bot update that added email support, more connectors and faster voice calls.
items.impact: If Chad's iPhone has an Action Button (15 Pro or later), one press after updating to 1.16 opens a voice chat with his Bots, a quicker way to hand off tasks hands-free.

items.headline: Nashville Sheriff Daron Hall retires after 24 years; Metro Council to appoint interim in November
items.summary_html: Davidson County Sheriff Daron Hall's last day was Monday, Oct. 19. He is leaving for the private sector after 24 years as sheriff and 35 years with the department, months after being elected to a seventh term. Metro Council will appoint an interim sheriff in November, and the office will be on the ballot next year.
items.connections: Fox17 notes the Tennessee Department of Correction will also have an interim leader after Commissioner Frank Strada resigned following Christa Pike's failed execution, so both the county jail system and the state prison system are changing leadership at the same time.
items.impact: This is a Davidson County office, so Chad won't vote on it from Hendersonville, and it doesn't change anything about his drive or his kids' schools.

items.headline: fal and Black Forest Labs release FLUX 3 Max video model at 75% off for three weeks
items.summary_html: fal announced FLUX 3 Max at 1:34 PM CT on Oct 19. It is a post-trained video model built with Black Forest Labs, and fal says it is tied for first in image-to-video quality on independent benchmarks, making a 10-second 720/768p clip in about 12 seconds. fal says it is 75% off for the next three weeks.
items.impact: It's a cheap way for Chad to test a top-ranked image-to-video model on his stills while the discount runs, through fal's pay-per-use pricing.

items.headline: Runway's video and image plugin is now available inside Grok Bot
items.summary_html: Runway said at 1:21 PM CT on Oct 19 that its MCP plugin now works in Grok Bot. You add Runway from Grok Bot's Marketplace and sign in with a Runway account, with no API key. Generations bill to your Runway credits, and Runway says agents can use models like Gen-4.5, Seedance 2.5, Kling, Veo 3.1, GPT Image 2 and Nano Banana Pro depending on your plan.
items.connections: It follows Grok Bot's Oct 16 update that added new connectors, and Pika's Oct 16 plugin that put its tools inside ChatGPT. Video makers are moving their tools into chat agents.
items.impact: Chad uses Grok Bot and Seedance 2.5 for his video work, so he could now call Seedance, Kling and Veo through Runway without leaving Grok Bot. It costs Runway credits, which is a separate bill from his X Subscription.

items.headline: Lavrov visits Tehran as Iran blames U.S. for Strait of Hormuz insecurity
items.summary_html: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov arrived in Tehran on Monday for his first visit since the U.S.-Iran war began in February, saying his talks are aimed at preventing a return to large-scale war. At a joint news conference, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the war and the U.S. blockade of Iran's ports are the main source of insecurity in the region. Iran says its seven-day ceasefire proposal for a phased reopening of the strait, which President Trump rejected last month, is still on the table.
items.connections: The U.K. navy counted 10 attacks on ships in and near the strait last week, making October the worst month for shipping attacks there since March, and crude stayed above $105 a barrel after nearing $110. Russia's mediation push comes days after Trump paused new U.S. sanctions on Russia, and as Iran-backed Houthis step up attacks on Saudi Arabia.
items.impact: Gas prices for Chad's drives to church and around Hendersonville stay tied to whether the strait reopens. CBS reports talks between Tehran and Washington are at a standstill, so there is no near-term relief at the pump.

items.headline: Apple sets Oct. 28 'Pro and Tell' event, with a touchscreen MacBook Pro expected
items.summary_html: Apple sent invites Monday for a 'Pro and Tell' product event in Los Angeles on Oct. 28, its second launch event this month after the smart-home 'Welcome Home' release. Analysts and Bloomberg's Mark Gurman expect Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pro with an OLED display, more M6 Macs including an iMac, and an OLED iPad mini; Apple itself has not said what it will show.
items.connections: It lands days after iPhone Duo pre-orders opened and sold out into late January, making this one of Apple's busiest fall launch stretches on record.
items.impact: Chad runs Logic Pro on a Mac, so any new MacBook Pro or iMac is worth a look before upgrading; nothing is announced until Oct. 28, and prices aren't known yet.

items.headline: Colts' Sauce Gardner week-to-week with calf strain from Titans game
items.summary_html: Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner is week-to-week with a mild left calf strain, confirmed by MRI Monday, after leaving Sunday's 26-20 loss to the Titans and not returning, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported. He isn't expected to miss an extended period.
items.connections: The injury came in the Titans' first win of the season and a day before the Colts fired GM Chris Ballard.
items.impact: Titans-adjacent NFL news for Chad as a fan; no effect on his daily life.

items.headline: Russian drone strike on Kharkiv region park kills six, including three children
items.summary_html: A Russian drone struck the central park in Nova Vodolaha, Kharkiv Oblast, at about 4:30 p.m. local time Monday, killing six people, including three children and an infant in a stroller, according to regional head Oleh Syniehubov and Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi. Fifteen people were injured, seven of them children, and a nearby cafe was damaged. Prosecutors say early findings point to a Geran-3 jet-powered drone and have opened a war crimes investigation.
items.connections: The strike came hours after an overnight Russian barrage on Kyiv and the power grid that left more than half a million families without electricity. It also lands as President Trump defends a pause on new Russia sanctions and criticizes Zelenskyy.
items.impact: No direct effect on Chad's daily life in Hendersonville; it bears on the U.S. policy debate over Russia sanctions and aid to Ukraine heading into the midterms.

items.headline: Trump signs order creating NIH women's health division and White House task force
items.summary_html: President Trump signed an executive order Monday, alongside First Lady Melania Trump, directing HHS to set up a Women's Health Division at the National Institutes of Health within 90 days. The division will coordinate research on conditions that uniquely or disproportionately affect women, including heart disease, cancer, endometriosis, menopause and infertility. The order also creates a White House Women's Health Task Force co-chaired by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, with HHS covering its administrative costs.
items.connections: The order came on a day Trump headed to a Kansas rally, two weeks before the Nov. 3 midterms, as new polls show his approval at record lows. The order doesn't name a new funding amount for the division.
items.impact: This is a research and coordination order. It doesn't change insurance coverage or costs for Chad's family right now.

items.headline: VideoGen unveils Model 1, aimed at ten-minute multi-shot videos from one prompt
items.summary_html: San Francisco startup VideoGen announced Model 1 on Oct 19. It plans and generates multi-shot videos up to ten minutes long from a single prompt, keeping characters and locations consistent. Its CEO puts quality at about 80% of Seedance 2.5 at less than half the cost, but no benchmarks or prices are out yet. Rollout starts with private partners, and applications are open for a $1 million pool of free credits.
items.impact: It isn't open to the public yet, so nothing changes for Chad today. The free-credit program could be worth applying to for his story projects.

items.headline: Metro Council to vote on MNPS application for $4.2 million state SRO grant
items.summary_html: Metro Council will vote this week on whether MNPS can apply for the Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security's School Resource Officer grant, which pays up to $75,000 per school for a dedicated school police officer. If awarded, the $4.2 million would support SROs in 56 Nashville schools. All MNPS middle and high schools have at least one SRO now, but only seven of the district's 73 elementary schools do.
items.connections: This follows the Oct. 16 reporting on how few MNPS elementary schools have a dedicated SRO. The state grant program began after the 2023 Covenant School shooting, and Metro Police issued a school safety report in March after the Antioch High School shooting. An earlier WSMV video caption put the grant at $4.8 million, but the updated article says $4.2 million.
items.impact: Chad's kids attend MNPS at Creswell, so the vote could bring more officers to district schools, including elementary schools that have none today. The article doesn't say which schools would get them.

items.headline: Meta says the first phase of its Prometheus AI supercluster in Ohio is complete
items.summary_html: Meta says the first phase of Prometheus, its gigawatt-scale AI supercluster in New Albany, Ohio, is finished and was used to train its Muse foundation models, including Muse Wonder. Meta engineers wrote that the site runs Nvidia GB200 and GB300 NVL72 racks, with Vera Rubin racks coming next, and is being scaled toward roughly 1 million GPUs. They also reported a 99 percent drop in training interruptions since mid-2025.
items.connections: Meta reports third-quarter earnings on October 21, when investors are watching its AI spending, and its next supercluster, Hyperion, is being built in Richland Parish, Louisiana.

items.headline: Home Bound Meals silent auction open in Hendersonville through Oct 31
items.summary_html: The 2026 Home Bound Meals Program silent auction is taking online bids through BiddingOwl until 11 AM on Saturday, October 31. An in-person event runs 7 to 11 AM that morning in the Hendersonville High School cafeteria, with $5 admission that includes a pancake breakfast and some paper-bid-only items.
items.impact: It's a local Hendersonville community fundraiser Chad can bid on from home, and the in-person breakfast on October 31 is a low-cost family outing at Hendersonville High.

items.headline: Rays lead ALCS 3-2, can clinch World Series trip vs. Guardians in Game 6 tonight
items.summary_html: The Tampa Bay Rays lead the Cleveland Guardians 3-2 in the ALCS after a 3-1 win in Game 5, and Game 6 is tonight at Tropicana Field at 7:08 PM CT on TBS, truTV and HBO Max. Freddy Peralta starts for Tampa Bay. If Cleveland wins, Game 7 would be Tuesday at 7:08 PM CT in Tampa Bay.
items.connections: The winner faces the Milwaukee Brewers, who swept the Dodgers 4-0 in the NLCS, in the World Series starting Friday, Oct. 23. A Rays-Brewers Series would match two franchises that have never won a World Series.
items.impact: First pitch is 7:08 PM CT tonight on TBS, so it's an evening watch from Hendersonville.

items.headline: Meta apologizes for suspending the No Kings coalition's Instagram account during protests
items.summary_html: Meta apologized after its automated security systems wrongly suspended the No Kings Coalition's Instagram account during the Oct. 17 protests. Meta said a burst of automated profile and post reading by an AI tool, about four times normal volume, set off its bot-traffic protections; the account was restored, but organizers were locked out of admin access for several hours.

items.headline: Houthi missile strike on Yemeni army camp in Shabwa kills at least 53
items.summary_html: Iran-backed Houthi rebels hit a government military training camp in southern Yemen's Shabwa province with ballistic missiles Monday, killing at least 53 soldiers, Yemeni military officials told AP. The provincial government said about 200 recruits were wounded and the toll may rise; the Houthis acknowledged targeting the camp. Yemen's leadership council head Rashad al-Alimi promised a "firm response."
items.connections: AP describes the Houthi-government fighting as a widening front in the Iran war that began in February. The Houthis have also been striking Saudi airports and oil sites, and the Houthi-run health ministry said a Saudi-led airstrike in Saada killed at least nine people Sunday.
items.impact: No direct effect on Chad. AP notes the Houthis hold ground near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a shipping route that matters for world oil supply.

items.headline: Microsoft pulls out of Nscale's planned Essex AI data centre over grid delays
items.summary_html: Microsoft has ended its role as anchor tenant at Nscale's planned Loughton, Essex AI data centre after the local grid operator said power may not be available until the early-to-mid 2030s instead of late 2026. The site was meant to house about 23,000 Nvidia chips for Azure. Nscale says it is still committed to the £2bn project and is looking at other power sources, and its Microsoft contracts in Norway, Portugal and the US are unaffected.
items.connections: It's another sign that electricity, not chips, is now the main limit on AI buildouts, the same pressure behind Musk's posts about SpaceX struggling to rent extra inference compute.
items.impact: No direct effect on Chad. Power shortages like this are part of why AI tools keep hitting usage caps and price changes.

items.headline: Mavs unsure if Santi Aldama will play in Wednesday's opener at Houston
items.summary_html: Dallas coach Dusty May said he doesn't know yet whether Santi Aldama will be available for Wednesday's season opener at Houston. Aldama, acquired this offseason, had arthroscopic surgery on his right knee in March while with Memphis and sat out all four preseason games. Dereck Lively II also remains sidelined, while Kyrie Irving came through the preseason without new injuries.
items.connections: Lively, the Mavs' other injured big man, also faces a 5 PM CT deadline today on a rookie-scale contract extension. With both out, Dallas is short on healthy frontcourt players heading into the opener.
items.impact: The opener is Wednesday, Oct. 21, at Houston at 7:30 PM CT, and the home opener is Saturday, Oct. 24, against San Antonio.

items.headline: Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefonica and Vodafone plan joint bid for EU satellite-to-phone spectrum
items.summary_html: Four of Europe's biggest carriers signed a letter of intent Monday to explore a joint bid for the EU's upcoming Mobile Satellite Services spectrum, used for direct-to-device service to ordinary phones. They would build the ground network and coordination functions in Europe and pick a satellite partner later, without investing in a constellation themselves. The carriers say it does not replace their existing satellite partnerships.
items.connections: The EU is rewriting how it awards the 2 GHz satellite band, whose current rights expire in May 2027, and the U.S. ambassador to the EU has warned of retaliation over plans seen as favoring European operators. SpaceX is building Starlink Mobile around 2 GHz spectrum in the U.S., so this group could become a rival bidder in Europe.
items.impact: This doesn't affect Chad's phone service in Tennessee; it's a European licensing fight.

items.headline: Father arrested after leaving 4-month-old alone in running car on Broadway, police say
items.summary_html: Metro Nashville Police say Jordan Hayley, 25, left his 4-month-old daughter alone in the front seat of a running car near Broadway while he went into Jason Aldean's Kitchen + Rooftop Bar over the weekend. Officers found the infant after breaking up an argument outside the bar; the baby was reunited with her mother. Hayley is charged with leaving an unattended child in a motor vehicle and child neglect, with a court review set for Friday.
items.connections: The case was reported Monday after officers were called to a dispute outside a Broadway honky-tonk Sunday; it adds to recent downtown public-safety coverage, including the Whiskey Row security homicide court dates already on the feed.
items.impact: This is a downtown Broadway arrest story and does not affect Chad's Hendersonville commute, MNPS schools, or drive to Priest Lake.

items.headline: Mavericks waive Dwight Powell after 12 seasons
items.summary_html: Dallas waived center Dwight Powell on Monday morning ahead of the NBA roster deadline, likely ending his 12-year run with the franchise. He played 768 games for Dallas and averaged 6.5 points.
items.impact: One of the longest-tenured Mavs is gone before Wednesday's 7:30 PM CT opener at Houston. If unclaimed, he clears waivers that same day.

items.headline: Saleh: Titans' offense 'hit or miss' after Colts win; Browns visit Sunday
items.summary_html: A day after the 26-20 comeback win at Indianapolis, Titans coach Robert Saleh said the offense has been hit or miss and that Cam Ward has to play at a higher level, while praising a defense that had six sacks. Saleh did not explain why cornerback Alontae Taylor was inactive and said the staff will decide his status. Tennessee hosts the Cleveland Browns this Sunday at Nissan Stadium.
items.connections: Safety Kevin Winston Jr. was out against the Colts with a quad injury and Tyjae Spears was questionable with a knee injury, so this week's injury reports will show their status for Cleveland.
items.impact: The Browns game is at home at Nissan Stadium in Nashville this Sunday; the team's report didn't list a kickoff time.

items.headline: Nvidia wins AI cloud startup Modal as an early customer for its Vera CPU
items.summary_html: Modal, which rents computing power to AI developers, said it will start using Nvidia's new Vera central processor to host AI agents, after relying only on Intel and AMD chips. Modal said early tests showed the Nvidia chip doubled how much work agents could get done, and it will run Vera alongside Intel and AMD in a mixed fleet. Nvidia has told investors it expects at least $20 billion in Vera sales this fiscal year.
items.connections: It came the same day Amazon announced TorchNeuron to pull PyTorch developers toward its Trainium chips, as Nvidia and its rivals fight over AI computing on both the GPU and CPU side.

items.headline: Free small business forum in Hendersonville Tuesday morning
items.summary_html: A free Small Business and Entrepreneurs Forum runs from 9 to 10:30 AM on Tuesday, October 20, at the Sumner County Innovation Center at 735 East Main Street in Hendersonville. It covers local permits and zoning, business consulting and training, growth resources, and networking. Registration is required, and spots were still open.
items.impact: It's a free local event close to home in Hendersonville, which could be useful if Chad is weighing freelance or side business work. Otherwise it doesn't affect his schedule.

items.headline: Colts fire GM Chris Ballard a day after blown lead to Titans
items.summary_html: The Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday morning, one day after Indianapolis blew a 13-0 halftime lead and lost 26-20 at home to the previously winless Titans. Assistant GM Ed Dodds will run personnel for the rest of the season, and coach Shane Steichen's staff will report to ownership. Ballard finishes 72-82-1 in nearly 10 seasons, with two playoff trips and no division titles.
items.connections: The firing follows the Titans' 26-20 comeback win in Indianapolis on Sunday, Tennessee's first win of the season. The Colts are now 2-4 and face the 5-0 Vikings next.
items.impact: The Titans' first win directly triggered front-office upheaval for an AFC South rival, which Chad will feel as a Titans fan. It doesn't touch his budget, church work, or family.

items.headline: Supreme Court won't revive plea deal for alleged 9/11 mastermind Khalid Sheikh Mohammed
items.summary_html: The Supreme Court on Monday declined, without comment, to hear appeals from Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, Mustafa al-Hawsawi and Walid bin Attash seeking to reinstate 2024 plea deals that would have given them life sentences instead of a possible death penalty. Then-Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin withdrew the deals days after they were reached, and the D.C. Circuit upheld that move in August. The men are scheduled for military commission trials at Guantanamo in 2028, and Justice Brett Kavanaugh did not take part in the Mohammed petition.
items.connections: On the same order list, the court also turned away former NLRB member Gwynne Wilcox's challenge to her firing by Trump, leaving in place a D.C. Circuit ruling that the president can remove NLRB members at will.
items.impact: This doesn't touch Chad's daily life directly.

items.headline: Amazon's TorchNeuron lets PyTorch code run on its Trainium chips without rewrites
items.summary_html: Amazon's Annapurna Labs is releasing TorchNeuron, free and open-source software that lets developers run PyTorch code on Amazon's Trainium AI chips with a single configuration change, Reuters reports. Amazon says more than 30 early customers are using it. The move targets the software advantage Nvidia has built with its CUDA tools.
items.connections: Google is pursuing the same goal with better PyTorch tools for its own AI chips, as cloud companies try to pull developers away from Nvidia.
items.impact: This is cloud-infrastructure news and doesn't directly touch Chad's day-to-day tools.

items.headline: Councilman calls for Jefferson Street redesign after nearly 90 crashes this year
items.summary_html: Metro Councilman Jacob Kupin wants safety changes on Jefferson Street just north of downtown Nashville, where MNPD data shows nearly 90 crashes so far this year. He says the wide lanes encourage speeding and is asking transportation officials to consider safer crossings, a possible road diet, and HAWK pedestrian signals like the one on 8th Avenue.
items.connections: It follows a Fox17 report on Oct. 16 about the same push for safer pedestrian crossings on Jefferson Street, and comes as Nashville neighbors elsewhere, like South Nashville ahead of the I-24 Choice Lane work, are also asking for safer roads.
items.impact: This is a North Nashville street safety issue and doesn't directly touch Chad's usual drive from Hendersonville to Priest Lake.

items.headline: Amazon backs a proposed 960 MW, 12-reactor nuclear plant in Indiana
items.summary_html: Amazon, utility AEP and X-energy signed a joint development agreement to study a 960-megawatt plant of twelve 80 MW Xe-100 small modular reactors at the former Breed coal plant site in Sullivan County, Indiana. AEP would own and run it, while Amazon funds development and would buy the power under a long-term contract if it's built.
items.connections: It's part of the big tech race for power to run AI data centers, alongside Google's and Microsoft's energy deals.
items.impact: This doesn't directly affect Chad.

items.headline: Russian barrage cuts power to more than half a million in Ukraine; Zelenskyy says no early warning came
items.summary_html: Russia hit more than 10 Ukrainian energy facilities overnight into Monday, leaving more than half a million people without power, heat and running water, Zelenskyy said. Officials in Kyiv said a 21-year-old woman was killed as Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles at the capital region. Zelenskyy said partners again gave no early warning; Secretary of State Marco Rubio repeated Monday that the US hasn't stopped sharing intelligence.
items.connections: The strikes came a day after Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia, setting fire to an oil export terminal and depot in St. Petersburg. They also follow Trump's waiver of US sanctions on Moscow and an energy truce he demanded that, per AP, came to nothing.
items.impact: This doesn't directly touch Chad's life in Hendersonville.

items.headline: Google pitches its 780 MW Minnesota data center as a grid upgrade, but skeptics question the costs
items.summary_html: Google and Xcel Energy say a proposed 780-megawatt data center in Pine Island, Minnesota, would finance 1,400 MW of wind, 200 MW of solar and 300 MW of battery storage without shifting costs to other customers. Google would pay for at least 75 percent of its contracted capacity even if it uses less, plus exit fees if it leaves early. The deal still needs approval from the Minnesota Public Utilities Commission, and some experts warn utilities have an incentive to overbuild.
items.connections: It's one of several big-tech power stories today, alongside Amazon's backing of a 960 MW nuclear plan in Indiana and Microsoft pulling out of a UK data center over grid delays.
items.impact: Who pays for data center power is a live question for utility bills everywhere, including Tennessee, though this specific deal is in Minnesota and doesn't change Chad's bill.

items.headline: MiniMax launches M3.1 Flash, the stealth Space Bunny model
items.summary_html: MiniMax officially released M3.1 Flash on Oct 19 and confirmed that Space Bunny, the anonymous model that topped OpenRouter and OpenCode usage charts for more than a week, was an early version of it. MiniMax says it is nearly three times faster and about 70% cheaper to run than its predecessor, with strong agent, coding, computer-use and cybersecurity scores, priced at $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.60 per million output tokens. It is live on the MiniMax API and MiniMax Code, free for a limited time on OpenRouter, OpenCode and Cline, and MiniMax says weights come later with a Pro model to follow.
items.impact: No direct effect on Chad's video work; it is a cheap text and coding model, not a video model. It adds to the price pressure that keeps AI tools getting cheaper.

items.headline: Tenstorrent raises $1.5B at a $6.2B valuation to challenge Nvidia
items.summary_html: AI chipmaker Tenstorrent, led by CEO Jim Keller, closed a $1.5 billion Series E on Oct 19 at a $6.2 billion post-money valuation, more than double its late-2024 mark. Trace Capital and Innovation X led the round, joined by ARK Invest, Fidelity, Morgan Stanley, Sandisk, T. Rowe Price and Tether Investments. The money funds volume manufacturing of its Galaxy servers, which run open-weight language and video-generation models, plus its RISC-V chip designs.
items.impact: Nothing changes for Chad right away. More competition for Nvidia could make running AI models, including video generation, cheaper over time.

items.headline: Apple buys AI audio startup Samplab, likely to boost Logic Pro
items.summary_html: Apple acquired assets of Zurich-based Samplab and is hiring some of its staff, according to the EU's Digital Markets Act acquisitions register, with the deal notified in June. Samplab made AI tools that split songs into stems, detect and edit chords, and change individual notes inside recordings. Terms weren't disclosed, and Samplab has shut its site and refunded subscribers.
items.connections: Logic Pro already added AI stem splitting in 2024, and this follows Apple's earlier purchase of AI podcast company Huxe this year.
items.impact: Chad uses Logic Pro for church music and production, so note-level editing inside chords would be directly useful; Apple hasn't announced any Logic feature from the deal yet.

items.headline: Tesla asks shareholders to re-elect Musk, Denholm and Straubel at Dec. 3 meeting
items.summary_html: Tesla filed its proxy statement Monday for its Dec. 3 annual meeting, asking shareholders to re-elect CEO Elon Musk, Chair Robyn Denholm and director JB Straubel to three-year terms. Reuters reports that none of the 12 tranches of Musk's roughly $1 trillion 2025 performance award has been earned yet, and that Tesla worked with the SEC on a new voluntary voting framework for retail investors.
items.connections: The filing lands two days before Tesla reports Q3 earnings on Wednesday, Oct. 21, and days after the next-gen Roadster unveiling.
items.impact: No direct effect on Chad unless he holds Tesla stock; it doesn't change Model Y L pricing.

items.headline: Report: Treasury preparing private debt collectors and 2027 penalties for defaulted student loans
items.summary_html: The Washington Sun, citing five sources, reported that Trump administration officials are preparing to penalize borrowers in default on federal student loans next year, and that Treasury plans to hire private debt collectors, possibly as soon as November, though the plans are unlikely to be announced before the midterms. Some officials want to garnish wages and seize benefits such as tax refunds for the tax year ending April 15, 2027, while sources cautioned it could be delayed again. OMB and Treasury declined to comment, and the Education Department said it doesn't respond to fishing expeditions.
items.connections: Involuntary collections have been on hold since the Education Department delayed them earlier this year while new repayment plans were finalized. It comes the same weekend a Business Insider report described a PSLF borrower whose forgiven loans had payments reclassified, another sign of turbulence in federal loan programs.
items.impact: This targets loans in default, so it only touches Chad if any of his federal loans are in default. Staying current or in a qualifying plan while pursuing PSLF keeps him out of the garnishment and tax refund offset programs described here.

items.headline: Musk says he'll give one SpaceX share to every U.S. child next year
items.summary_html: Elon Musk posted on X early Monday that in 2027 he will give one of his own SpaceX shares to every child in America, calling it "the first of many." CNBC puts the value at about $10.5 billion, based on roughly 72 million U.S. kids and Friday's $146.03 close. Musk gave no details on eligibility or how the shares would be delivered.
items.connections: The post came a day after Anthropic said it would put 5% of its shares into a public benefit fund, and Musk replied that shares should go directly to the public. SpaceX stock rose about 2% to 3% Monday morning ahead of its Q3 results on Tuesday, Oct. 20.
items.impact: If it happens as described, Chad's two sons, both under 18, would each be in line for one share, worth about $146 at Friday's close. There's no sign-up process or timeline yet, so there's nothing to do for now.

items.headline: Lithuania investigates failed arson attack on a Starlink gateway site in Vilnius
items.summary_html: Someone tried to set fire to Starlink antennas and a control unit at a Vilnius site SpaceX rents, around 2 a.m. Sunday; the fire was put out quickly with minor damage and no service disruption. Lithuanian officials call it Russia-linked sabotage aimed at Ukraine's military communications, and police said Monday the suspects are still at large.
items.connections: It follows arson attacks on Starlink sites in Bulgaria on Oct. 10 and in Poland in September, and comes amid the dispute over Starshield speed limits on Ukraine's military terminals.
items.impact: This doesn't directly affect Chad.

items.headline: Trump endorses Netanyahu ahead of Israel's Oct. 27 election
items.summary_html: Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on social media Sunday, calling him a "Great Warrior Prime Minister" in the Iran fight. He again threatened to "soon finish the job" against Iran and said that if anyone else wins, "America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so." Netanyahu thanked Trump; Israelis vote Oct. 27, their first national election since the Oct. 7, 2023 attack.
items.connections: AP reports Trump had held back the endorsement for months as the two leaders' Middle East strategies diverged, and many Israelis are disappointed with the inconclusive end of the Iran war that began in February.
items.impact: This doesn't directly touch Chad's life.

items.headline: Trump defends Russia sanctions waiver and says Zelenskyy doesn't want the war to end
items.summary_html: On Truth Social Sunday, Trump defended his order blocking Russia sanctions days before they took effect, saying he doesn't want to drive Russia "away from the bargaining table." He also wrote that Zelenskyy "doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did," pointing to Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries. Zelenskyy told NBC's Meet the Press the waiver "will hurt Ukraine" and said he has kept talking with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
items.connections: The waiver is drawing Republican pushback too: The Hill reports Speaker Mike Johnson said he warned the White House of "unintended consequences." It also comes alongside Trump's Oct 9 plan for Russia to supply diesel to global markets as fuel prices stay high from the Iran war.
items.impact: No direct effect on Chad's loans or taxes. The administration's stated reason for its Russia energy moves is high fuel prices, which hit his drives to church and a tight budget.

items.headline: Rays beat Guardians 3-1 in Game 5, lead ALCS 3-2 heading home
items.summary_html: Drew Rasmussen allowed one run over seven innings and Tampa Bay won 3-1 in Cleveland on Sunday to take a 3-2 lead in the ALCS, its first lead of the series and its second straight win. The Rays scored once in each of the first three innings, and Bryan Baker closed it for his fifth save of the postseason.
items.connections: The winner faces the NL champion Brewers, who swept the Dodgers 4-0 in the NLCS, with World Series Game 1 in Milwaukee on Friday. Neither the Rays nor the Brewers has ever won a World Series, so a Rays pennant would guarantee a first-time champion.
items.impact: ALCS Game 6, with the Rays leading the Guardians 3-2, is tonight in St. Petersburg around 7:08 PM CT on TBS and truTV, and Game 7 if needed is Tuesday; World Series Game 1 is Friday, October 23 at 7 PM CT on FOX.

items.headline: Kings' Ben Simmons tears Achilles, likely out for the season
items.summary_html: Sacramento Kings guard Ben Simmons tore his Achilles tendon in a live drill at practice on Sunday and will have surgery, the team announced. The injury is likely season-ending for the 30-year-old three-time All-Star, who signed a one-year, $3.5 million deal with the Kings in September after sitting out last season. He averaged 10.5 points in two preseason games.
items.connections: The NBA regular season tips off Tuesday, and Sacramento is also without centers Maxime Raynaud and Dylan Cardwell for a few weeks, according to NBC Sports.
items.impact: This is league-wide NBA news and doesn't affect the Mavericks or Chad's life directly.

items.headline: Titans rally from 13 down to beat Colts 26-20 for first win
items.summary_html: Tennessee erased a 13-0 halftime deficit at Indianapolis on Sunday, using a 58-yard Chimere Dike punt return, a blocked-punt touchdown and two late Joey Slye field goals to win 26-20 and improve to 1-5. It was Robert Saleh's first win as Titans coach; the defense forced three turnovers and had six sacks. Tyjae Spears played through his knee issue, while Kevin Winston Jr. (quad) was inactive.
items.connections: Last week's injury report listed Spears as questionable and ruled out Winston Jr. for this game. The win snapped Tennessee's six-game losing streak against the Colts.
items.impact: The Titans' next game is at home against the Browns on Sunday, Oct. 25 at noon CT.

items.headline: Whiskey Row security staff charged in 2021 death of DJ Barrett due in court Tuesday
items.summary_html: Six men who were working security at Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row on Lower Broadway are set to appear in court Tuesday and face a jury trial Dec. 7 in the death of 22-year-old Dallas "DJ" Jordan Barrett. Police say security pulled Barrett to the ground and held him down after an altercation on Aug. 16, 2021, and he died of asphyxiation. Metro Police ruled the death a homicide, and the men charged face reckless homicide and aggravated assault counts.
items.impact: This is a downtown Nashville court case and doesn't directly affect Chad's commute, schools, or Hendersonville.

items.headline: Anthropic commits 5% of shares to a Public Benefit Fund
items.summary_html: On Oct 18 Anthropic said that, subject to stockholder approval, it will commit 5% of its shares to a new wholly owned Public Benefit Fund LLC, with the board able to add 2 more percentage points for each 50% rise in company value above a set baseline. The fund can make large nonprofit donations or direct distributions, including for AI labor-market impacts, and its equity will not be used for lobbying or political giving. Combined with founder and employee equity pledges, Anthropic says roughly 20% of shares would be dedicated to public good.
items.connections: Musk responded by recommending shares go directly to the public, then posted early Oct 19 that SpaceX would give one share to every U.S. child in 2027. Both moves sit in the same week of AI-company philanthropy headlines ahead of Anthropic's reported IPO timing.
items.impact: Indirect for Chad: it is a major Anthropic corporate story on the Claude maker he follows, not a product change. The labor-market framing may matter later if the fund funds worker programs, but nothing here changes Claude access, PSLF, or his day-to-day tools.

items.headline: Emergency roadwork blocks two of three I-65 northbound lanes in Goodlettsville
items.summary_html: TDOT reported emergency roadwork on northbound I-65 near mile marker 96 in Goodlettsville at about 9:18 Sunday morning, with two of the three northbound lanes blocked and traffic slowing. The cause wasn't clear, and TDOT had not given an estimated time for all lanes to reopen.
items.connections: This is separate from the weekend I-65 closure between I-40 and I-440 near Hamilton Avenue, which TDOT said would reopen by 5 AM Monday. TDOT also posted that the I-65 southbound on-ramp from Long Hollow Pike (exit 97) closes tonight from 8 PM to 5 AM for milling.
items.impact: Mile marker 96 sits between the Vietnam Veterans Blvd (exit 95) and Long Hollow Pike (exit 97) interchanges, so northbound slowdowns there touch the drive home to Hendersonville after church. The southbound trip to Priest Lake isn't affected.

items.headline: Metro Nashville steps up warnings to unpermitted short-term rentals
items.summary_html: Metro Nashville sent warning notices to 14 properties last week for operating short-term rentals without a valid permit, compared with 21 notices in all of the previous month. Most cited properties are near downtown in Council Districts 5 and 21, and owners have until mid-November to act or face further enforcement. AirDNA counts more than 11,000 advertised short-term rentals in Nashville versus fewer than 7,050 active permits.
items.impact: This is a Davidson County codes issue and doesn't directly affect Chad in Hendersonville.

items.headline: Market & Melody Festival coming to Gallatin Nov. 7 to benefit foster children
items.summary_html: The Market & Melody Festival is set for Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, from noon to 6 p.m. at 1616 Long Hollow Pike in Gallatin. It will feature live music on a main stage, handmade crafts and boutique vendors, food trucks, and family activities. Proceeds benefit Love From Music City, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit serving Middle Tennessee foster children.
items.impact: It's a free-afternoon family option close to home in Sumner County, and the organizers are also inviting musical artists to take part, which could interest a church music director. It's on a Saturday, so it doesn't conflict with Sunday service or Thursday rehearsal.

items.headline: PSLF borrower told his loans were forgiven, then had 15 payments reclassified
items.summary_html: Business Insider reports that Donald Knierim, a 71-year-old former Metra employee, retired after his Federal Student Aid dashboard said in November 2025 that no more payments were required, only to later have 15 payments relabeled non-qualifying. His servicer says about 18 more months of payments of roughly $470 are due, and his account is now delinquent while a reconsideration request is pending. The Education Department says it is committed to crediting every qualifying payment, and has attributed some recent payment-count corrections to Biden-era coding errors.
items.connections: It follows reports this month of PSLF payment counts being paused over data issues and a backlog of PSLF Buyback applications. In September, eight state student-loan ombudsman offices asked the Education Department and Congress for stronger PSLF oversight.
items.impact: Chad's PSLF progress depends on payment counts being right, so it's worth saving screenshots of his StudentAid.gov tracker and every servicer notice. The story says borrowers can file complaints with the department's ombudsman or a state ombudsman.

items.headline: Predators beat Blues 5-2 as five different players score
items.summary_html: Jonathan Marchessault (on a penalty shot), Filip Forsberg (his first of the season), Adam Edstrom, Ryan O'Reilly and Jack Drury scored as Nashville beat St. Louis 5-2 Saturday at Bridgestone Arena. Juuse Saros made 24 saves, and the Preds have earned points in six of their eight games.
items.connections: The win closed a three-game homestand that included Thursday's shootout loss to San Jose.
items.impact: The Preds are off until Thursday, Oct. 22, when they play at Boston at 6 PM CT to start a two-game road trip that continues in Pittsburgh.

items.headline: Mavs face 5 PM deadline on Dereck Lively extension before Wednesday opener at Houston
items.summary_html: The Mavericks have until 5 PM CT today to sign center Dereck Lively II to a rookie-scale extension; without one he plays this season on his $7,239,131 fourth-year salary and could become a restricted free agent next summer. Lively has not been medically cleared after foot surgery and missed all four preseason games. Dallas opens the regular season Wednesday, Oct. 21, at Houston at 7:30 PM CT.
items.connections: Kyrie Irving, playing again after missing all of last season, scored 18 in Friday's 135-111 preseason loss to the Hawks and is projected to start the opener alongside Cooper Flagg.
items.impact: The opener tips at 7:30 PM CT Wednesday, an evening game Chad can catch from home.

items.headline: Poll: Trump approval hits record low of 33% as Democrats lead House ballot
items.summary_html: A Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll of 2,545 adults taken Oct. 9-13 puts Trump's approval at 33% and disapproval at 66%, his lowest in the poll across both terms. Among likely voters, Democrats lead Republicans 52% to 44% on the generic House ballot. Only 28% approve of his handling of the economy.
items.connections: The poll lands about two weeks before the Nov. 3 midterms, as Trump campaigns in Kansas and Republicans push back on his Russia sanctions waiver, per The Hill.
items.impact: The midterms will decide which party controls Congress, and Congress sets student loan, tax and health care law, including any future PSLF changes. Chad votes in Tennessee's races on the same ballot.

items.headline: Early voting in Davidson County far outpaces 2022 under new congressional maps
items.summary_html: Davidson County recorded 28,070 early voters in the first three days of early voting, compared with 1,813 in the same period of 2022, and Shelby County saw 33,205, up from 17,784, according to Fox 17. Early voting began Wednesday under new congressional district lines approved in May that split parts of both counties. Pastors held a Souls to the Polls event Saturday at the Bordeaux Library polling site.
items.connections: This ballot also includes the governor's race, and the redistricting that divided Davidson and Shelby counties has drawn criticism from community leaders quoted in the story.
items.impact: Chad votes in Sumner County, and Tennessee early voters can use any early voting site in their own county, so he doesn't need to go to his assigned precinct during early voting.

items.headline: Man shot outside Super 8 on Old Hickory Boulevard in Whites Creek; shooter drove off
items.summary_html: Metro Nashville police were called around 5:45 Saturday to a Super 8 hotel on Old Hickory Boulevard off Interstate 24 in Whites Creek, where one man was shot. Police said his injuries are not life-threatening. The suspect drove away, and police have not released a description of the suspect or vehicle.
items.impact: This is in north Davidson County off I-24, away from Chad's I-65 and Vietnam Veterans Boulevard route, so it doesn't directly affect his drive.

items.headline: Man hit and killed by CSX train near East Campbell Road in Madison
items.summary_html: Metro Nashville police say a man was struck and killed by a CSX train on the tracks near East Campbell Road in Madison just after 10 a.m. Saturday. The engineer told police the train was going 35 to 40 mph and sounded its horn several times, but the man stepped into the middle of the tracks as the brakes were applied. Police described him as a white man who appeared to be in his 30s, and the medical examiner is helping identify him.
items.impact: Madison sits between Hendersonville and downtown along Chad's usual route, but this was a single incident on the rail line and police reported no lasting road closures.

items.headline: Kentucky man killed in head-on crash on Springfield Highway in Nashville
items.summary_html: A 50-year-old Adairville, Kentucky, man died after his Chevrolet S-10 pickup crossed into the southbound lanes and hit a Subaru Forester around 8 p.m. Friday in the 1400 block of Springfield Highway, Metro police said. The 26-year-old Subaru driver was taken to TriStar Skyline Medical Center with critical injuries, and police said there were no signs either driver was impaired.
items.connections: It is the second deadly traffic crash Metro police reported from Friday night, after a pedestrian was killed crossing Bell Road.
items.impact: Springfield Highway is in north Davidson County, off Chad's usual I-65 route, and the scene has cleared, so it doesn't affect his drive.

items.headline: Davidovich Fokina rallies past Jodar to win Shanghai Masters
items.summary_html: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina beat fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar 1-6, 7-6(5), 6-4 in Sunday's Shanghai Masters final for his first ATP Masters 1000 title. He rises to a career-high No. 13 in Monday's rankings, while the 20-year-old Jodar moves up to No. 11 and sits ninth in the race to the ATP Finals in Turin.
items.connections: Jodar reached the final by beating Daniil Medvedev 6-3, 6-4 in Saturday's semifinals, and Davidovich Fokina upset top seed Alexander Zverev in the other semifinal.
items.impact: No direct effect on Chad; it closes out the Shanghai event where Medvedev's run ended in the semifinals.

items.headline: Man found shot dead in apartment on 16th Avenue North near TSU homecoming parade
items.summary_html: A man with at least one gunshot wound was found dead inside an apartment in the 900 block of 16th Avenue North on Saturday morning, after emergency crews were called shortly after 8 a.m., WSMV reported. Nashville Fire Department crews declared him dead at the scene. As of about 10:30 a.m. there was no information on possible suspects, and police were still working out what led to his death.
items.connections: The scene is a few blocks from Jefferson Street, where crowds gathered Saturday for the TSU homecoming parade that already has Jefferson Street and the I-40 west Jefferson exit closed, and WSMV said it asked TSU about homecoming security.
items.impact: This doesn't touch Chad's Hendersonville routes or his Sunday drive to Priest Lake, but North Nashville near TSU is busy and partly closed today.

items.headline: Pedestrian killed crossing Bell Road in Nashville
items.summary_html: A 43-year-old man died Saturday morning after an eastbound Acura Integra hit him as he crossed from the north to the south side of the 1100 block of Bell Road, Metro Nashville Police said. He died at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, and police said there were no signs of impairment at the scene. His name hasn't been released while police notify family.
items.connections: It comes a day after a Metro councilmember pushed for safer pedestrian crossings on Jefferson Street, another sign that pedestrian safety is a live issue in Nashville this week.
items.impact: This doesn't directly touch Chad's Hendersonville routes, though Bell Road is in the southeast Nashville area not far from the drive toward Priest Lake.
